L3 (used on browsers such as Chrome or Firefox, even on Linux) allows up to 1080p depending on the service, generally less. L1, currently available only on proprietary systems such as Android, allows higher resolutions. Windows works with Microsoft's PlayReady, same problem but we're never getting that.
L1 requires trusted system, just like anti cheats. Other despicable DRMs like Denuvo for video games work just fine under Proton.

Basically, not having Widevine L1 on Linux means being stuck at 720p on Netflix.
I despise DRM but I think that, just like anti-cheat software, it’s a barrier to the widespread adoption of Linux. I don't care about piracy, I do it a lot, but I don't think everyone is able to give up Netflix.

The workflow that has worked for me:

1. Run the vendor app on Windows (or in a VM with USB passthrough) and capture with USBPcap, or with usbmon on the Linux host if it's a VM.
2. Change exactly one thing at a time (color red, wait, color blue, wait, brightness down) and write down when.
3. Diff the packets between those actions. The bytes that change with your action are the parameters, the ones that never change are the header.
4. Replay the packets from Linux with pyusb or hidapi, then turn that into a small driver or a udev + script setup.

I built usb-rea to automate steps 3 and 4: it reads the pcapng, groups the packets by action, infers the command layout (headers, counters, length fields, checksums) and writes a Markdown report (every claim linked to Wireshark frame numbers) plus a standalone pyusb driver. It's a CLI and also an MCP server, so an AI assistant can drive the analysis. I check it in CI against devices that are already documented: from NZXT Kraken X captures it recovers the fan command byte for byte as liquidctl sends it, and the same for the SteelSeries Rival 100 tables from rivalcfg.

https://github.com/emirmrkaljevic/usb-rea

Before reversing anything, check OpenRGB, liquidctl and the device's GitHub issues first, someone has often done it already. Happy to look at a capture if anyone has a device stuck on Windows.","creator_id":32691369,"community_id":721021,"removed":false,"locked":false,"published":"2026-11-25T08:02:22.753047Z","deleted":false,"nsfw":false,"ap_id":"https://programming.dev/post/59881358","local":false,"language_id":0,"featured_community":false,"featured_local":false},"creator":{"id":32691369,"name":"emirmrkaljevic","banned":false,"published":"2026-11-23T14:12:54.382483Z","actor_id":"https://programming.dev/u/emirmrkaljevic","local":false,"deleted":false,"bot_account":false,"instance_id":137032},"community":{"id":721021,"name":"linuxhardware","title":"LinuxHardware","description":"A community where you can ask questions about what hardware supports GNU/Linux, how to get things working, places to buy from (i.e. they support GNU/Linux) and so on.
